subject: Clarification: control boundaries & KMS evidence for ISO/FedRAMP intake
messages:
From: Emma Reyes <emma@brightaudit.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:03:12 -0400
Subject: Clarification: control boundaries & KMS evidence for ISO/FedRAMP intake

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending the initial intake. We're preparing the scoping questionnaire for Parcelly Systems' upcoming certification and I have a few clarifying questions so we scope the evidence collection correctly: 

1) Boundary: We need the logical and physical boundary document that shows which services, accounts, and regions are in-scope for both ISO 27001 and FedRAMP. Can you confirm whether the Hosted API and Dedicated pools are in the same scope?

2) Key Management: Please provide the KMS architecture diagram and the rotation/retirement schedule for keys used for customer data encryption. We will need precise Control Evidence for KM-1 / KM-2 (or equivalent).

3) Network segmentation: A short legend + diagram showing segmentation between control plane, inference pools, and customer VPCs. In particular, do you have documented firewall rules or NAC policies we can reference?

4) Third-party dependencies: Any attestation or subservice provider list (e.g., cloud provider regions used, monitoring vendors). For FedRAMP we annotate these for inheritance.

5) Evidence owners: Who on your side will be responsible for producing the artifacts (PDFs, runbooks, logs)? We'll need name + email + backup owner.

6) Timeline: Parcelly's audit window is currently 2027-07-05 to 2027-07-09. Can you indicate when we can expect the artifacts? Ideally we ask for a snapshot export by 2027-06-15.

Attachments: none at the moment.

If it helps, I'm happy to hop on a 30-minute call this week to walk the team through the exact evidence templates.

Best,
Emma
Senior ISO Auditor
BrightAudit LLC
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Clarification: control boundaries & KMS evidence for ISO/FedRAMP intake

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) Boundary: Hosted API + Dedicated pools are in-scope for Parcelly's engagement. Private deployments (customer-managed on-prem installs) are out of scope for this activity unless Parcelly specifically commissioned them. I'm attaching the current iso_network_boundary.pdf which shows logical components and AWS accounts we include.

2) Key Management: Vivek will upload the KMS diagram and rotation schedule. High level: we use a customer-key-per-customer model for hosted keys with envelope encryption; root keys are rotated annually and data keys rotate per rolling schedule (30/90 days depending on tier). We'll provide the CSV export for rotation history.

3) Network segmentation: Attachment includes a simplified legend; we also have a firewall rules excerpt. For the audit we'll produce a sanitized firewall rule export.

4) Third-party dependencies: See page 3 of the boundary doc for cloud provider accounts and monitoring vendors. We will also include the current ATO/inheritance list.

5) Evidence owners:
- KMS and cryptography: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com> (backup: Marissa Cole)
- Network & infra: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com> (backup: Soojin Lee)
- Controls mapping & policies: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>

6) Timeline: We can target a first drop by 2027-06-10 and final snapshot by 2027-06-18. If BrightAudit can provide the evidence list template, we'll align to it.

Next step: propose a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the attachments and confirm any redaction needs.

Attachments: iso_network_boundary.pdf (diagram), network-segmentation-legend.png (diagram)

Thanks,
Soojin
Head of Compliance

Thanks, Soojin — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups before the call:

- For rotation: the CSV you mentioned should include key IDs, creation date, last-rotation date, next-rotation target, and owner.

I'll send our evidence list in a Drive folder (we'll give you subfolders for ISO/FedRAMP/SIG). If you can drop the initial artifacts to the folder and ping me, we'll mark them as 'received' in our tracker.

Call: Monday 2027-05-17 10:00 AM ET work for you?

Emma

Hi Emma / team — following up with the requested KMS specifics and a short summary of where the artifacts will come from.

KMS architecture and ownership:
- We operate a multi-tenant strategy where each customer is issued a unique data key encrypted by a tenant-specific CMK (customer master key) in AWS KMS. CMKs are customer-scoped for hosted customers; Dedicated customers may bring their own keys (BYOK) or request a dedicated CMK from our account.
- Access to CMKs is controlled via IAM roles with strict condition keys; the CMK policy references team role ARNs.

Rotation schedule (attached: kms_rotation_schedule.csv):
- Master/root CMK rotation: annual, last rotated 2026-11-02
- Customer CMKs: rotated on a 90-day cadence by default; some high-tier customers are set to 30 days. CSV includes key_id,last_rotation,next_rotation,owner.comments

Evidence we will drop to the Drive folder:
- KMS diagram (kms-diagram.png) and CSV export (kms_rotation_schedule.csv)
- KMS policy extracts (sanitized) showing CMK policy statements and IAM role ARNs (kms_policy_excerpt.txt)
- Rotation job logs (exported snapshot for the relevant window)

Network segmentation notes:
- Firewall rules are managed in our infra repo; we'll extract rule IDs with effective timestamps and sanitize IPs. Attached is network-segmentation-legend.png for quick reference.

If this looks good, I'll upload the artifacts to the Drive link you provide and notify the thread.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
